verified: The real public ACP process passes complete and deliberately truncated responses from a controlled HTTP model. The first text arrives before the terminal frame, independently of final persistence.
The complete reply is written once to the canonical transcript and arrives as two client chunks without a repeated final copy.
The incomplete response emits a protocol error without committing the provisional text or dispatching the unvalidated write_file.
Four existing standard wire fixture families preserve exact text across input fragmentation. The public Chat Completions test and SDK also verify two Chinese chunks end to end.
Qoder's window for physical retry retains its legacy terminal-buffered text behavior. Auxiliary summary requests never feed the visible assistant stream.
limits: External SDK and Chat Completions loopback on macOS, with standard wire fragmentation checked using recorded fixtures. No installed editor or real-account acceptance.
Linux build is an amd64 container debug test. No long-duration buffer or memory acceptance.
